origins.section: A Processor Is Code javac Runs During the Compile, and What It Adds Is New Source Files
An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line
Processing Runs in Rounds, and a Generated File Is Processed in the Next One
The Filer Creates Each File Once and Never Replaces a Class That Exists

recorded.pass:q-classpath-discovery: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-classpath-discovery: Section 'A Processor Is Code javac Runs During the Compile...', callout 'Discovery changed after Java 21': "With that jar only on `-cp`, javac 21 ran the processor and printed a note ... javac 25, given the same command, ran no processor and failed with the `cannot find symbol` above." Summary: "javac 25 no longer runs one found only on the class path." Reference table: "processor jar with a services file, on `-cp` only | javac 21: runs, with a note; javac 25: doesn't run".

recorded.outcome:q-missing-location: Section 'An Error Reported at the Element Makes javac Point at the User's Line': "A message of kind `ERROR` fails the compile: javac exited with 1 and wrote no class files." and "Without the element argument the location is lost: javac printed `error: @Command class needs a public no-arg constructor` with no file and no line, and in a large build you can't tell which class." recorded.prompt:q-state-across-rounds: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-state-across-rounds: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-state-across-rounds: Section 'Processing Runs in Rounds...': "Every file created in a round is an input of the next round ... Rounds go on until one creates nothing, and then a last round runs with no inputs and `processingOver()` true." and "a processor called in one round is called in every later round, including the last, even with no annotations for it, and that javac creates the processor object once per compile, not once per round. That is why `found` carries the commands from round to round." Round log shows 3 rounds (sources, generated class, empty/over). 3 + 2 = 5 follows.
recorded.prompt:q-add-a-method: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-add-a-method: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-add-a-method: Design Note: "code that wants generated behaviour must call a generated class (`CommandIndex.create`) or extend one." Summary: "what it adds are new files that compile with the sources." The page's own example (CommandIndex, a separate generated class the user code calls) matches. The page does not show reading fields to build JSON, but the approach itself is supported.

recorded.outcome:q-add-a-method:b: Section 'The Filer Creates Each File Once...': "Nor can a processor edit a class in place: `Element` has only getters." Design Note: "The API offers no way to change a class the developer wrote" -> javac adds nothing to <Name>'s supertypes. Partly true: the page endorses generating a superclass ("The `Filer` javadoc's alternative is to generate a superclass or a subclass of the user's class"; "or extend one"), so an instance toJson() in a generated class does work if the user's class extends it; only the 'javac adds to supertypes' rationale is false. The page states this implicitly, not in so many words.
